model: Holdco Head Office cash flow (dividend and fee income less overhead, net interest and tax) capitalised at cost of equity, cross-checked to SOTP adjusted NAV (engine route)

sotp_nav_crosscheck.basis: Company's Adjusted NAV methodology (H1-2026 interim p.34): listed stakes at quoted price x economic interest, MPIC at 2023 delisting tender price (PHP 2,600/share post 500:1 reverse split), FPM Power at investment cost. Re-marked from 30-Jun-2026 to 9-Oct-2026 by each stake's own price and FX move.
sotp_nav_crosscheck.note: MPIC at the 2023 tender price is conservative: FY2025 MPIC contribution was US$250.6m, so the US$1.2bn mark is <5x recurring contribution. The NAV therefore understates look-through value, which partly offsets the holdco discount the market applies.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR (27.5%) diverges >30% from equity 5yr CAGR (6.9%): EPS compounds off the COVID-depressed FY2020 base (0.046). The model's own base growth path (4.5% fading to 3%) is set from Head Office dividend income, which has been flat at US$305-324m for three years after the FY2023 step-up.
historical_growth.notes: 'fcf' CAGRs are the Head Office net operating cash inflow (the valued stream: FY2020 ~117m, FY2022 ~155m, FY2025 225.7m), not consolidated FCF. Consolidated revenue is Indofood + MPIC + PLP turnover and is not the holdco's revenue.

scenario_narratives.base: Upstream dividends grow ~4% a year in USD: Indofood's rupiah dividend compounds mid-to-high single digits but loses 2-3pts a year to rupiah depreciation; MPIC's dividend rises with Maynilad tariff resets and MPTC toll volumes; PLDT's dividend is roughly flat as capex falls to the mid-50bn-peso range; Philex's Silangan mine adds a small new stream from 2026. Head Office overhead and interest stay near-fixed, so the net stream grows a little faster than gross income. Value lands ~17% below the market-marked SOTP NAV, i.e. the holdco discount persists but at the narrow end of its decade range.
scenario_narratives.bull: The catalysts land: Silangan ramps and Philex resumes dividends, Maya's 2026 IPO and further Maynilad-style listings crystallise value and lift upstream payouts, MPIC's capex cycle peaks and its dividend steps up, and PLDT de-levers toward 2.0x net debt/EBITDA and restores payout growth. Peso and rupiah stabilise, the Head Office refinances the 2027 bond cheaply after S&P's BBB upgrade, and the market prices the holdco at a lower cost of equity.
scenario_narratives.bear: EM FX and sovereign stress: Indonesia's negative outlook turns into a rupiah slide, PLDT trims its dividend to protect its balance sheet, and MPIC holds cash for its capex programme, so dividend income falls ~4% in FY2027 and grows only ~2% thereafter. Refinancing the US$350m 4.375% 2027 bond and floating bank debt at higher rates lifts Head Office interest, and Salim-family related-party capital allocation (FPM Power top-ups, Maya) consumes more Head Office cash. The holdco discount widens back toward its 50-60% historical norm.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value First Pacific on what it actually receives. Consolidated cash flows belong largely to Indofood and MPIC minorities and lenders; what reaches 0142.HK shareholders is dividend and fee income at Head Office, less overhead and Head Office interest. That stream is capitalised at a USD cost of equity, with Head Office debt left inside the flows rather than subtracted again, and the result is cross-checked against the company's own market-marked SOTP adjusted NAV. The market-marked NAV (HK$6.51) caps the base case: a holdco paying ~US$85m a year in overhead and interest, with Salim-family control and related-party flows, deserves a discount to NAV; the base case implies ~17%, the narrow end of the 17-66% decade range.
key_risks_to_valuation: Rupiah and peso depreciation: about 90% of NAV is in IDR/PHP assets and every 1% move in both currencies moves adjusted NAV by tens of millions of USD (FY2025 AR FX sensitivity table).
Dividend policy at investees: PLDT (high leverage, 2.56x net debt/EBITDA) and MPIC (capex supercycle) control most of the upstream cash, and First Pacific does not set their payout.
Refinancing of the US$350m 4.375% bond due September 2027 and ~US$1.1bn of floating bank loans.
Holdco discount persistence: NAV growth has not reliably turned into share-price growth; the discount was 48-66% from 2016 to 2023.
Philex is held at its 30-Jun-2026 PSE price (no live quote on Yahoo), so the SOTP cross-check is stale on that line (~8% of gross asset value).

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 4.68-6.74 HKD. Stake prices (INDF.JK, PHI ADR) and FX (USDIDR, USDPHP, HKD=X) from the same API, 2026-10-09/10.
data_sources.financials: FY2025 Annual Report (Head Office Cash Flow, Contribution and Profit Summary, Adjusted NAV Per Share, Ten-year statistics); H1-2026 Interim Report (Adjusted NAV at 30 June 2026, Head Office debt profile, dividend and fee income US$138.8m vs 132.5m); historical Head Office cash flow tables FY2018-FY2024 annuals.

inputs.sbc_source: Not deducted: the valued stream is Head Office cash flow; subsidiary SBC (consolidated US$5.7m FY2025, nil equity-award taxes) is already borne before dividends reach Head Office. Head Office share-award purchases (US$0-6.7m/yr) sit in the capex/net-investment line.
inputs.fx_note: USD->HKD 7.8472 (Yahoo HKD=X, 2026-10-10 close); HKD is pegged in the 7.75-7.85 band. Parity check: ADR FPAFY (1 ADR = 5 shares) converted at 7.8472 sits within ~1.5% of the HKEX quote at inputs.price_as_of (ADR spread/timing).
inputs.share_count_basis: 4,262.1m ordinary shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (H1-2026 interim, Adjusted NAV table). Dilutive awards/options are immaterial (diluted EPS 7.07 US cents vs basic ~7.07). No buybacks since FY2022; held flat.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD (the stream is USD-reported, Head Office debt is USD): US 10y ~4.3% + blended equity risk premium ~6.7% for Indonesian/Philippine look-through exposure (Indonesia sovereign outlook revised to negative early 2026) and holdco complexity/related-party governance = 11.0% base; 10.0% bull, 12.5% bear. Net debt is NOT subtracted: net cash interest on Head Office debt (US$1,340.7m at 30 Jun 2026) is already deducted inside the stream, so subtracting it again would double-count.
inputs.lease_treatment: Head Office lease payments are immaterial and sit in 'Others' financing; no lease charge modelled.
inputs.nci_treatment: Handled structurally: only dividends actually upstreamed to Head Office are valued, so the ~60% of consolidated profit attributable to non-controlling interests (NCI US$1,119.9m FY2025) never enters the stream.
inputs.notes: MODEL: First Pacific is a holding company whose consolidated statements (USD 10.2bn revenue, 13.0bn gross borrowings, NCI 8.7bn) describe Indofood and MPIC, not the shareholder's claim. Routed per dcf-methods SKILL.md to the holdco row and valued on the flow that actually accrues to 0142.HK shareholders: Head Office dividend and fee income (FY2025 US$310.9m; FY2024 305.3; FY2023 324.1; FY2022 225.9; FY2020 189.9; FY2017 185.5) less Head Office overhead (19.2), net cash interest (65.3) and tax (0.7) = Head Office net operating cash inflow US$225.7m (FY2025 AR Head Office Cash Flow table, line ~4341). Capitalised at cost of equity with net debt held at zero (interest already inside). Owner-FCF on consolidated FCF would be meaningless here (consolidated FCF 360m is mostly MPIC/Indofood cash owed partly to minorities and to subsidiary lenders). Cross-check: company-style SOTP adjusted NAV re-marked to 9-Oct-2026 market prices = US$3,534m = HK$6.51/share (see sotp_nav_crosscheck); the base value sits ~17% below it, inside the 17-66% decade range of the holdco discount. 'capex' line = recurring Head Office net investments (FPM Power top-ups, Maya, LTIP trustee funding: 46.4m FY2025, 17.8m FY2024).

base.margin_rationale: 'Margin' = (dividend & fee income - HO overhead - net cash interest) / dividend & fee income; FY2025 actual 72.8%. Overhead (~US$19m) and interest (~US$65m on ~US$1.34bn net debt at 4.5% blended) are near-fixed, so the margin rises slowly as upstream dividends grow.
base.capex_rationale: 6% of dividend income (~US$19m/yr) = recurring Head Office net investments, midway between FY2024 (17.8m) and FY2025 (46.4m, which included Maynilad shares distributed in specie).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the stream is concentrated in two EM sovereigns (Indonesia outlook negative; peso and rupiah already cut H1-2026 recurring profit 3%), Head Office gearing is 1.41x, and governance/related-party risk is real. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent catalysts (Silangan, Maya IPO, PLDT de-levering, FX stability) to land together. Base 50% on a 9-year record of dividend income at or above US$165m and three straight years above US$300m.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
